about: Why your phone dies in the cold. Factory #27, backlog row 31, slug coldbattery. One hard idea: a phone that shuts off in the cold usually isn't dead; cold slows the battery's chemistry and raises its impedance, so under load the voltage drops and the phone shuts itself off to protect its parts; warm it up and battery life returns to normal. Primary sources (read 2026-11-10): Apple Support 'If your iPhone or iPad gets too hot or too cold' (https://support.apple.com/en-us/118431, published May 14, 2026); Apple Support 'iPhone battery and performance' (https://support.apple.com/en-us/101575, published Jun 1, 2026); Google Pixel Phone Help 'Check & understand your Pixel's temperature' (https://support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/15679416); Samsung US 'Galaxy Battery Care & Maintenance' and 'About Battery' (samsung.com/us/support/galaxy-battery/); Battery University BU-502 (updated 2021-10-27) and BU-410 (updated 2022-03-01). Planned silences: 0.8 s after 'protect itself.' (dip: phone goes black, OFF stamp), 1.0 s after 'comes back.' (hero: screen relights, BATTERY LIFE RETURNS stamp). Narration-led: record the voice first and key every visual beat to its word times.

lines.text: Your phone isn't dead. It's cold.
So why does your phone die in the cold?
lines.say: So, why does your phone die in the cold?

lines.text: Check your weather app. Under 32 degrees?
lines.say: Check your weather app. Under thirty-two degrees?

lines.text: Apple designs iPhones for 32 to 95 degrees.
lines.say: Apple designs iPhones for thirty-two to ninety-five degrees.

lines.text: Cold slows the chemistry inside the battery.
At 0°F, a typical battery gives about half its capacity.
lines.say: At zero degrees, a typical battery gives about half its capacity.

lines.text: Its voltage drops, so it shuts off to protect itself.
But warm it up, and the battery life comes back.
lines.say: But, warm it up, and the battery life comes back.

lines.text: Keep it in an inside pocket.
And let it warm up before you charge it.
lines.say: And let it warm up, before you charge it.

lines.text: Has yours died in the cold?
lines.say: Has yours died in the cold?
